html:
The battle in the hills of northwest Vietnam, from March to May 1954, in which the Viet Minh crushed a French garrison and ended French rule in Indochina.

By 1953 the First Indochina War had dragged on for seven years. The French commanders built a fortified base in the valley of Điện Biên Phủ, supplied by air, to block Viet Minh routes into Laos. They were sure the Viet Minh could not bring heavy guns over the mountains.

General Võ Nguyên Giáp proved them wrong. Tens of thousands of porters and soldiers hauled artillery and anti-aircraft guns into the hills around the valley. When the attack began on 13 March, the guns shut the airstrip within days. Strongpoint after strongpoint fell. On 7 May the garrison surrendered, and some 11,000 French Union soldiers were taken prisoner.

The next day the Geneva Conference turned to Indochina. Vietnam was split in two at the 17th parallel, setting the stage for the Vietnam War. It was a rare defeat of a European army by a colonial independence army in open battle.
sum: The battle in the hills of northwest Vietnam, from March to May 1954, in which the Viet Minh crushed a French garrison and ended French rule in Indochina.
